paragraphs.text: Dear sisters and elders, I was able to cross the border today, got into the Bulacan Zone. I enjoyed seeing almost all the missionaries in that zone. It was fantastic.

I ran out of time, wasn't able to see a couple of you, but pretty much everybody else I got to, and it was great to see that almost all of you are doing very, very well and making good progress on your goals and are really focused on your purpose here in the mission field. Well done, well done.

Our zone interviews start tomorrow, and I'll be having a personal interview with each missionary through messenger video. If you're not already connected to me on messenger, please send me a request on messenger to S-F space Hughes.

That's S-F and then a space and then my last name, and I'll be able to reach out to you for our interview, and also I want to have your contact info anyway. I'll also be just doing one district per day, and the reason for that is I want to have more time to visit with you and understand how you're doing.

Also, here's a warning, please be prepared to teach me a three to five minute lesson on either one, two, or three. So at the beginning of our call, I'll give you a heads up as to which lesson I'll be asking you to teach me. It'll be either lesson one, lesson two, lesson three.

You need to teach me a lesson that's at least three minutes long, but not longer than five minutes. So something between three and five minutes, and you need to teach me in English. Alright, 100% in English.

There's reason for that. A, I don't speak Tagalog, so I want to be able to understand what you're teaching me, but also I want to be able to report to Sister Hughes how you're doing on your English language development.

Now, this shouldn't alarm any of you. You should all be pros at doing this online teaching, and I'm excited to see your skill. I'm excited to see your power. I'm excited to see how well you do. So let's go have a great experience with this, and don't let it bother you. Just, you know, just step up to the plate and swing the bat, and let's get better.
Alright, let's jump into our topic today. Smooth stone number four. Smooth stone number four is measurement and accountability.
Thomas S. Monson is of course an amazing human being, president of the church, prophet for our time, and a remarkably effective manager and builder of people and organizations.

He had a famous quote, and I actually got a copy of this quote signed by him that sits inside of a frame in my office back in the U.S. The quote goes like this. Part of it is in Preach My Gospel, but I'm going to give you the whole quote.

Quote, "When we deal in generalities, we will never succeed. When we deal in specifics, we will rarely have a failure. When performance is measured, performance improves. When performance is measured and reported back, the rate of improvement accelerates." Close quote.
Again, that's from Thomas S. Monson. I want to break that down into the four parts that stand out.

Number one, President Monson saying, when we deal in general stuff, when we don't get specific, we're probably going to fail. I mean, quite honestly, I've seen that in my life. I've seen that in other people's lives. I've seen that in businesses.
I've seen that in businesses that I've bought to turn around. The first thing I noticed is they weren't measuring anything specific, and so they didn't get any specific good results.
It goes on. The next stanza of this quote and it says, when we deal in specifics, we will rarely have a failure. Why would that be?

Well, when you deal in specifics, you figure out exactly how well you're doing specifically on the steps that lead to the outcome you want, and if you're not doing well, you can get better. But if you don't even know what the specifics are because you're being too general, you can never improve them. That's why generality leads to failure and specifics lead to success.
Now, the third part of this, which is in your Preach My Gospel, when performance is measured, performance improves, and it's true. Literally, just measuring something.

You want to change how many calories you eat a day? Just start writing down everything you eat. You don't even need to make a deal about reducing it. Just the very act of writing down in a little notebook everything you eat right after you eat it will cause you to begin to eat less and better food. Interesting.

Another way this can be manifest to you very, very easily is to write down how much money you spend on each thing you spend it for. So you keep a little notebook. You spend 50 pesos on this. You write down the date, the time, 50 pesos on X, whatever it was.

And if you keep absolute strict measurement of what you're spending your money on, I flat guarantee you will spend less money and the money you spend, you will spend smarter because when performance is measured, performance improves.

Now, the fourth part of this, when performance is measured and reported back, the rate of improvement accelerates. This is key because what President Monson is teaching us here is that when we measure performance and then we're holding ourselves accountable about that, we don't just get better, we get better faster. And that's what we all want, right? We don't want to get better slower. We want to get better faster.

So again, when we deal in generalities, we will never succeed. When we deal in specifics, we will rarely have a failure. When performance is measured, performance improves. When performance is measured and reported back, the rate of improvement accelerates. We can thank President Monson for that amazing insight.
Bottom line, we measure everything because if you want something to get better, you start with measuring it.
Now, in the mission field, there's basically two things that matter. And so when I became the mission president here, I immediately began measuring these two things.
Number one, actions that you can take that are fully under your control that lead toward the outcome that you want. So I instituted what we called the ITA or the invitation to act.

Because all the other key indicators were indicators that needed the other person to exercise their agency in the right way for us to be able to have a positive outcome. But the invitation to act simply said, I'm going to invite someone to take some action and they can say no or they can say yes, but I'm going to count that because I did what I could do.

The second thing that we measure is the results we get from the actions we take. So one, you measure the actions we take that we can control and then we measure the results we get from the actions we take.

As missionaries, our only fundamental act that we can fully control is that invitation to take action. And you can talk, you can read about this in chapter 11, but we want to invite somebody to increase in light and intelligence, which they can only receive from God.

And as they receive that light and intelligence from God, that leads them to God as the covenant spoken of by section 84. So that is the one key action that we measure in this mission. We call it by different things now, but it's the same concept always.
What can we do to stimulate someone to actually move towards greater light and knowledge and intelligence so that they can be drawn back to the Father?

The result we're seeking is to have people gain their own testimony of the restored gospel of Jesus Christ so that they can know it's true and then they can make an agreement with God by baptism, by one who holds proper authority so that they can receive God's help to rise to the level of their potential.

It's really pretty simple. Those are the two primary things that I've always measured in this role as president of the mission. As you know, I've been laser focused on invitations and SMAs and baptisms.

There are other things that you'll measure in your own life as your life unfolds. You'll need to determine these things for yourself, but in your profession, in your family, in your civic responsibilities, in your church callings. There's going to be lots of different things, but keep focused in on the concept that anything that you measure, you can improve and if you can't measure it, you can't improve it.

Now, all proper measurements fall into two categories, leading indicators and lagging indicators. Now, a leading indicator is a behavioral action that you can take that will lead you toward the things you want, as I said earlier on. That's a leading indicator.

We know that if we did so many ITAs, it led to this many people wanting to be taught. If we taught this many lessons, we got this many people going to church and getting an SMA. If we had this many SMAs, we got this many baptismal date commitments. If we got that many baptismal date commitments, we got this many people baptized.

Those are indications, indicators rather, and they are leading and lagging. In fact, it's interesting that in many cases, a leading indicator in one sequence can be a lagging indicator in another sequence.
For instance, leading indicator, of course, the invitation to attend church, the lagging indicator, is that they attend church.

Now, attending church, we've proven through our research, is probably the key thing that allowed us to know that they would make a serious baptismal date commitment. SMAs became a leading indicator towards serious baptismal date commitments, which was the lagging indicator.
Then, serious baptismal date commitments became a leading indicator towards baptism, which in the end, in fact, became the lagging indicator.

We could take it farther. We could say baptism of a convert was the leading indicator towards getting endowed and sealed in the temple, which was the lagging indicator and so forth. I think you get the point.

If we're effective and we're diligent with our invitations, then we'll find people who choose to engage in the learning process. We'll call these people investigators or people who are investigating the church.

These people literally move through that process and measuring them at each step of the way allows us to analyze how well we're doing at missionary work, what's our skill level, what's our power level, what's our knowledge level.

Literally, as we see breakdowns, in other words, if we do this many invitations but only get that many people at church, we know we need to improve some element of our invitation process or something else, because we're obviously not getting the kind of results that we should be getting on our lagging indicator, which is to get people to church.
Anyway, let's move on here. Our ultimate goal, as I shared before, was to have people gain their own testimony of the truth.

If they're serious about the process, we ask them to choose a date to get baptized, and that would be based upon their obtaining a testimony. Then of course, as we continue to work with them and go through that process with the leading indicators, we ultimately get to that final lagging indicator when they come into the kingdom and they are baptized.
Bottom line here is we need to make sure that we are measuring all of these steps. As I said before, measurement precedes improvement.

In your work, you've got to find the start point for you. We've talked a little bit about getting referrals on messenger and there's different strategies. I'm monitoring all these things you're going back and forth on, on messenger, and I'm excited about what I'm seeing.

But it's really important that you're able to isolate these things into actions that you can measure because if you're not able to measure them, you may be led into a path that's not very productive and you won't know it until you've wasted a lot of time because you're not able to do any proper measurement.

Okay, now how do we establish leading and lagging indicators in our lives? We've talked about it in our mission. We've got it pretty much squared away in our mission because we've talked about these things for nearly three years now, but this should ring some bells for you if you were listening carefully to yesterday's message.
We talked about processes and systems. What are processes and systems? A process is a series of steps starting at the most basic that leads to the outcome you want.
A system is a collection of processes that lead to a more complicated outcome that you want. So as you think about that, a process basically is a documented set of steps which you could measure.

So each one of your steps in a process is either a leading or a lagging indicator and that allows you to create measurement steps in every process allowing you not just to be able to do it very, very well consistently and to teach others how to do it, but how to improve it by measuring how each step interacts with the next step.
In other words, does this work really been effective at connecting to the next step, moving me down that path?
The key for you, of course, is to be able to monitor yourself, your skill, your knowledge, your power so that you can actually see yourself getting better.
The human mind has an astonishing ability to, how to say this kindly, it has an astonishing ability to make you look like you're better than you are.

And so if you're not actually being particularly diligent in measuring, you'll get the idea that maybe you're doing better than you actually are. And we'll talk about that in accountability, but let me just wrap up measurement here.

Measurement is big. It's really big. And most of the people that I've seen fail in life who had the talent, who had the intelligence, who had the work ethic, they end up failing because they just don't take the time to measure what they're doing.
And people who don't measure their actions just don't really get very good at anything. But measurement without accountability is worthless.
And I know there are people in life, even people in the mission field, who will, well, they'll give measurements that are not actually true. I hate to say it, but I know it happens.

And the sad thing about that is it doesn't really help anybody. It certainly doesn't help the individual. If you're not honest with yourself about your measurement, then your measurements don't mean anything. And they can lead you and others into really bad decision making.

That's one of the reasons that we were so keyed in, so focused on having straight, honest answers in all the measurements we did back in the early days of the mission. Because we knew that without accurate measurements, our correlations from one indicator to the next would not be true.
So it's better to have honest measurement that is not what you want it to be than to have dishonest measurement that makes you look good, but just isn't real or true.

So if your goal is to look good, well, you can fake it for a while, but eventually you'll get shown up as not being as good as you were making yourself look. And that's pretty embarrassing and doesn't get forgotten very quickly. But also it robs you of time, time that you could have used to get better.

Now accountability is really just a mindset. And it's the mindset that you're going to honor the truth about your actions and your results. Growth really only gets going fast when a person begins to be super accountable.

If people, you know, this happens a little bit, people are a little soft on themselves. They kind of create a false picture of themselves to themselves. That's the interesting thing. Lying is bad, but lying to yourself is just stupid.

And yet all of us have done it at one time or another. Sometimes we just don't want to acknowledge the truth about ourselves in some aspect of our life. And we don't want to face the real facts about ourselves.
But in order for us to overcome what we don't like about ourselves, we have to own it. We have to face it. We have to be accountable for it.
And so in that act of accountability, we create the first step in removing ourselves from a place we don't like being or from a skill that we don't think is good enough or high enough.
And so as we look at this thing, we really want to get around the idea that we can't get away with denying reality. We can't get away with lying about reality.

There's a lot of people that do deny reality. I get that. I see it around me in my life. I see it around me in everything I do. But these people that do that, they're not really fooling anybody who's very tuned in. We just kind of feel sad for them, right?
So the bottom line is the universe is astonishingly accountable. I mean gravity, every law in the universe, every physical law just works. It works every time. There's just no exceptions.

And so when you really look at how you want to live your life, you want to live your life in conformity to the way nature actually works. And so you get this notion of saying, hey, I'm just going to be real.
Because while I can fake reality to myself, I can't fake it to others, and eventually there's going to be consequences to me faking reality.
And they're going to come out in the end, and usually a long time before the end, and you're just going to be able to say, wow, I really blew it because I wasted a ton of time.
So all of you are really young. I mean, you're 20 years old, little less, little more. So you're at the beginning of your life.
And if you decide right now that you're going to own your actions, you're going to own your results with a goal in mind that you can improve them and seek the help you need to get better and better.

As you do that, you will start to see massive improvement in your life. It'll be painful. I admit that it's painful to acknowledge reality when reality is not pretty. But if you want it to get pretty, the first step is acknowledging it where it is. And then it just starts getting better from there.
So there you have it, smooth stone number four, measurement and accountability. Tomorrow we will wrap up this series with smooth stone number five. I'm guessing that you'll like this one the best.

Good night and remember to hold yourself accountable. It's a myth that anyone else can hold you accountable. Mission president can't hold you accountable. I know there's mission presidents that think they can do it. They can't do it. I don't even try.
I mean, the reality of it is a missionary who won't hold himself accountable isn't going to go very far in the mission. He isn't going to go very far in life. And it's sad.

But the sooner he decides that it's him or her that needs to hold him or her accountable, that's when they're going to start making the growth and changing their world. So be accountable, hold yourself accountable, own it so you can grow it. I love you all. Talk to you tomorrow.
